recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. A future editorial cleanup may separately smooth the duplicated "is" if desired, but no FHIR-17035 source correction is needed.
issue_request: FHIR-17035 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Feed change request from the STU3 ballot asking the Bundle page to make clear that packaging resources in a Bundle does not itself provide List, Group, or Composition semantics. The approved resolution was to add a note under the List/Group/Composition enumeration saying those resources represent meaningful groupings, while a Bundle is only a container for transfer and storage.
initial_application: The Jira comment records svn 14395. Git-svn commit 50d2f5bd27854bd3d83b2d18d2fbad9e607b4284, "GF#17035 - clarification", maps to build@14395 and added the approved note to source/bundle/bundle-introduction.xml.
additional_context: Bundle is an active resource in source/fhir.ini, so source/bundle/bundle-introduction.xml is in current build scope. The current source still contains the requested semantic distinction immediately after the List, Group, and Composition enumeration. The inherited wording includes the grammatical duplication "merely is", but the implementer-facing meaning is clear and the reconciliation threshold does not justify an optional editorial-only source change for this issue.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because the current Bundle introduction already conveys the approved rule: List, Group, and Composition have meaningful grouping semantics, while Bundle is a transfer/storage container and does not add meaning merely by packaging resources.
